stem_book: If the mass of the nucleus accounts for almost the entire atomic mass, what does this indicate about the distribution of mass and charge within an atom? (a) Both mass and charge are uniformly distributed. (b) Mass is concentrated in the nucleus, and charge is spread over the entire atom. (c) Mass and charge are equally shared by electrons and protons. (d) All mass and charge are carried only by electrons.
key: b Mass concentrated in the nucleus; charge over the whole atom
derived: b Mass is concentrated in the nucleus, and charge is spread over the entire atom
correct_answer: b Mass is concentrated in the nucleus, and charge is spread over the entire atom
work: Nucleus (p + n) carries ~all mass; electrons (negative charge) occupy the whole atomic volume — only (b) fits
